newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries rise in London, rate hike seen receding.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries rise in London, rate hike seen receding.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries traded in London were stronger on Monday, buoyed by expectations that U.S. interest rates are on hold for the time being, traders said.
There is also a steady trickle of movement out of Europe into Treasuries, which is underpinning the stronger tone, they added. However, activity was relatively quiet, after the major moves last week.

"The Fed is out of the picture, the supply outlook is not so bad, and people are generally underinvested," said a trader at a U.S. bank in London. "The market should probably do better, and I'd be buying on dips."
The U.S. 30-year long bond was at 98-25, to yield 6.72 percent by 1000 GMT, compared with 98-21 in Tokyo and 98-22 at the New York close.
September T-bond futures were up 4/32 at 111-31 in automated trade.

Figures released last Friday showed May producer prices fell 0.3 percent, raising expectations that the July Federal Open Market Committee meeting will not see a rise in rates. Retail sales figures also fell for the third month, building up expectations further.
However, analysts said consumer price data, due for release on Tuesday could be disappointing since the market has persuaded itself that the economy is growing at a moderate pace.
May consumer prices are forecast to show a rise of 0.2 percent headline and underlying.

"There is certainly a bias towards disappointment," said Mark Capleton, international bond strategist at BZW in London. "Particularly as we have leading indicators, the Beige Book and the Philly Fed coming up. The period of thinking there is no need for a rate hike is going to be short."
The Beige Book will be released on Wednesday, and the Philadelphia Federal Reserve survey on Thursday.
Traders said technical indicators for Treasuries were bright in the short term, with any decline in the future likely to be stemmed at 111-12.
At the short end, September Eurodollars were up 0.005 at 94.145, while December was down 0.01 at 93.965.
